findings.claim: groundUnderBody (called through carView→visualPose for every car on every tick via carViews) calls groundAt without the module's scratch `ground`. groundAt's default parameter therefore allocates a new Ground object for every sample. The function also builds a throwaway `[-1e-6, -r.length]` array for every ramp. groundAt is the top allocation site in dust-bowl and the third in bends.
findings.evidence: src/sim/car.ts:206 `return { ts, hs: ts.map((t) => groundAt(track, car.x + fx * t, car.z + fz * t).h) };` takes the default at src/sim/track.ts:555 `out: Ground = { h: 0, gx: 0, gz: 0, ramp: null }`. The hot path already passes scratch: car.ts:370 and 580 `groundAt(track, car.x, car.z, ground)`, with the scratch at car.ts:324 `const ground: Ground = ...`. car.ts:201 `for (const a of [-1e-6, -r.length]) {` runs once per ramp per call. perf.json allocation per frame: groundAt 2118 B (bends) and 3975 B (dust-bowl, the top site); groundUnderBody 1168 B and 2295 B; visualPose 1197 B (dust-bowl). Only `.h` is read, straight away, and groundUnderBody never runs inside stepCars' use of `ground`, so the numbers can't change.
findings.suggestedFix: In groundUnderBody, pass the existing scratch: `groundAt(track, car.x + fx * t, car.z + fz * t, ground).h`. Replace the literal-array loop with two explicit pushes in the same order: compute t for a = -1e-6, then for a = -r.length, keeping the `Math.abs(t) < half` check. Same ts order and same hs values, so replays, bot laps and car poses are identical.

findings.claim: draw() calls raceView(r.world) on every rendered frame, but the world only changes in tick(). Each call allocates a distances array, the positions() order array with its sort and forEach closures and result array, and per racer a RacerView with `lapTicks.slice()`. Frames that ran no tick (any display above 60 Hz) and frames that ran several ticks still pay for it.
findings.evidence: src/game.ts:190 `ui.sync(raceView(r.world), r.curr);` runs in draw(), which frame() calls on every animation frame (game.ts:207) whether or not a tick ran. src/sim/world.ts:128-134: `world.racers.map(...)`, `positions(...)`, `world.racers.map((r, i) => racerView(...))`. src/sim/race.ts:96-112 shows map, sort with a closure, `new Array().fill`, and forEach. race.ts:121 has `lapTicks: r.lapTicks.slice()`. perf.json (bends): `sort ((native))` 968 B/frame and `map ((native))` 924 B/frame. Note: game.ts is also in open PRs #25 and #26.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `view: RaceView | null` to the Race record. Set it to null in tick() after stepWorld and in startRace, and in draw() use `ui.sync((r.view ??= raceView(r.world)), r.curr)`. raceView is a pure function of the world, so the UI receives identical values. Apply after #25 and #26 land, since both touch game.ts.
